newsitem.title: JAPAN: Saudi, Japan plan $1.2 bln petrochem plant scale-up.
newsitem.headline: Saudi, Japan plan $1.2 bln petrochem plant scale-up.

text.p: Saudi Basic Industry Corp (SABIC) and Japan's Saudi Petrochemical Development Co (SPDC) plan to expand output capacity at their joint venture Eastern Petrochemical Co at Al-Jubail by 2000, SPDC said on Friday.

The $1.2 billion expansion project includes the construction of an ethylene centre and ethylene glycol plant, and revamping of an existing liner low density polyethylene (LLDPE) plant, a SPDC spokesman said.
The new ethylene centre and ethylene glycol plant are expected to have annual production capacities of 800,000 tonnes and 450,000 tonnes, respectively, the spokesman said.
The revamping will raise the firm's LLDPE output capability to 700,000 tonnes a year from 400,000 tonnes, he said.
Eastern Petrochemical currently has output capacities of 1.5 million tonnes a year for ethylene and 800,000 tonnes for ethylene glycol.
The expansion plan is still in the preliminary stage, and a final agreement will be reached by the middle of 1997, the spoeksman said.
SPDC is owned by Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund and 63 private firms from the refining, petrochemical, auto, steel and transportation industries.
